lessons.title: Finding Wholesale and Liquidation Suppliers
lessons.body: To make money reselling, you need a reliable source of cheap products. Wholesale suppliers sell in bulk at lower prices, while liquidation suppliers sell off excess stock, customer returns, or bankrupt inventory at even deeper discounts. In Africa, start by visiting local wholesale markets like Balogun Market in Lagos, Kantamanto in Accra, or Toi Market in Nairobi. Walk the aisles, ask traders where they get their goods, and note prices. Many will source from importers who bring in containers from China, Dubai, or Turkey. Ask if you can buy a mixed pallet or a bale of assorted items. For example, a bale of 50 mixed-brand t-shirts might cost 500 Ghana cedis and resell for 20-30 cedis each, giving you 500-1000 cedis profit. Online, try Alibaba, but beware of scams; use Trade Assurance. Also check local Facebook groups like 'Lagos Wholesale and Liquidation' where sellers post clearance lots. For liquidation, look for stores closing down, or contact companies that sell off returned electronics. Always ask for a sample before committing to a large order. Build relationships: a good supplier will give you credit after a few cash purchases. Start small with 200-500 cedis, test what sells, then scale. Remember, your profit margin depends on buying low. A 30% margin is common; aim for 50% or more on trending items.

lessons.title: Thrift Store and Garage Sale Sourcing Strategies
lessons.body: Thrift stores (called 'bend-down' or 'second-hand' markets in many African countries) and garage sales are goldmines for resellers. In Kenya, Gikomba Market is famous for second-hand clothes; in Nigeria, Yaba and Oshodi have thrift stalls. Go early in the morning when new bales are opened. The best items are grabbed within the first hour. Bring cash and a large bag. Focus on quality brands: Zara, H&M, Nike, and Levi's sell fast on social media. Check for stains, tears, or missing buttons; minor flaws can be fixed and still profitable. A typical bale of 100 mixed clothes might cost 300-500 Kenyan shillings per piece, but you can sell individual pieces for 500-1500 shillings. For garage sales, scan local Facebook Marketplace, WhatsApp groups, and community notice boards. Estate sales often have household items, books, and electronics at low prices. Negotiate: offer to buy multiple items for a discount. For example, if a seller wants 2000 naira for a used blender, offer 1500 naira cash. Also, attend church jumble sales and school fairs. Always test electronics before buying. Clean and repair items before reselling; a little polish can double the price. Keep a notebook of what you paid and what you sold it for, so you know which thrift sources are most profitable.

lessons.title: Using Online Marketplaces for Sourcing
lessons.body: Online marketplaces let you source products without leaving your home. In Africa, popular platforms include Jumia (Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt), Kilimall (Kenya), and Takealot (South Africa). But for resellers, the best deals often come from Facebook Marketplace, Facebook groups, and WhatsApp Business catalogs. Join groups like 'Wholesale Suppliers Nigeria' or 'Nairobi Buy and Sell'. Post a 'wanted' ad: 'Looking for bulk phone cases, 100 pieces, budget 20,000 naira.' You'll get responses from suppliers. For international sourcing, use Alibaba, AliExpress, or DHgate. Always check seller ratings and reviews. Start with a small trial order of 10-20 units to test quality and shipping time. Shipping to Africa can take 2-6 weeks and incur customs duties; factor that into your cost. For example, a phone accessory that costs $1 on AliExpress might land at $2 after shipping and duty, and you can sell it for $5 locally. Also, use local classifieds like OLX (now Jiji in Nigeria) to find clearance lots. When buying online, use secure payment methods like PayPal or escrow. Never send money via Western Union to a stranger. Meet local sellers in person if possible, and inspect goods before paying. Keep records of all transactions for tax and profit tracking.

lessons.title: Negotiating Bulk Purchases
lessons.body: Negotiation is a skill that directly increases your profit. Before you negotiate, know the market price. Research online and visit multiple suppliers. If you're buying 50 units, ask for a 20-30% discount from the single-unit price. For example, if a supplier quotes 1000 naira per unit, offer 700 naira per unit for 50 units. Be polite but firm. Use phrases like 'I'm a regular buyer' or 'I can pay cash today.' Cash is king; many suppliers will lower the price for immediate payment. If they won't budge on price, ask for free delivery or extra items. Another tactic: buy in larger quantities. A supplier might give 40% off if you buy 200 units instead of 50. But don't overbuy if you can't sell that much. Start with a small order to build trust, then negotiate better terms on the next order. Also, consider group buying: team up with other resellers to pool money and buy a whole pallet at a lower price. Always get the agreement in writing via WhatsApp or email, including the price, quantity, and delivery date. If a supplier refuses to negotiate, walk away; there are many others. Remember, your goal is to get the lowest cost per unit without sacrificing quality.

lessons.title: Evaluating Product Quality and Profit Potential
lessons.body: Not every cheap product is a good deal. Before you buy in bulk, evaluate quality and profit potential. For quality, check materials, stitching, and functionality. For clothes, look at fabric thickness, seams, and zippers. For electronics, test charging, buttons, and screen. Ask for a sample if buying online. A common mistake is buying a large lot of low-quality items that won't sell. Instead, test a small batch first. For profit potential, calculate your total cost: purchase price + shipping + customs + packaging + social media ads. Then research the selling price on Facebook, Instagram, or Jumia. A good rule: your selling price should be at least double your total cost. For example, if a handbag costs 2000 naira landed, sell for 4000-5000 naira. Check demand: search hashtags like #handbagnigeria to see what's popular. Also consider seasonality: umbrellas sell in rainy season, Christmas decorations in December. Use a simple spreadsheet to track cost, price, and profit margin for each product. If an item doesn't sell within 2 weeks, discount it to recover cash. Focus on products with high turnover and repeat customers, like phone accessories, hair, or skincare. Avoid fads that die quickly.

lessons.title: Managing Inventory and Storage
lessons.body: Once you start buying in bulk, you need to manage inventory and storage to avoid losses. First, keep a record of every item: date bought, cost, quantity, and location. Use a notebook or a free app like Google Sheets or Zoho Inventory. Label boxes with purchase date and product name. Store items in a dry, clean space away from sunlight and pests. For clothes, use plastic bins or hang them to avoid wrinkles. For electronics, keep them in anti-static bags. If you don't have a spare room, use a locked trunk or rent a small storage unit (in Lagos, a 10x10 ft unit might cost 20,000 naira per month). But for most beginners, a corner of your bedroom works. Rotate stock: sell older items first (FIFO). Set a reorder point: when stock drops to 10 units, reorder. Track sales daily to know what's moving. If an item hasn't sold in 30 days, bundle it with a popular item or run a flash sale. Also, insure high-value inventory if possible. Keep your storage organized so you can find items quickly when an order comes in. A messy inventory leads to lost sales and wasted money.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of buying from wholesale suppliers?
options: B) You buy at lower prices per unit
C) They offer credit to everyone
quiz.explanation: Wholesale suppliers sell in bulk at lower prices per unit, which increases your profit margin.

quiz.q: Which of these is a popular wholesale market in Lagos, Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Balogun Market is a well-known wholesale market in Lagos, Nigeria.

quiz.q: What should you always ask for before committing to a large order from a new supplier?
quiz.explanation: A sample lets you check quality before buying in bulk.

quiz.q: What does 'liquidation' mean in the context of sourcing?
options: A) Selling off excess stock or bankrupt inventory at deep discounts
B) Buying new products from a factory
quiz.explanation: Liquidation refers to selling off excess stock, customer returns, or bankrupt inventory at low prices.

quiz.q: Which online platform is mentioned for finding wholesale suppliers internationally?
quiz.explanation: Alibaba is a global online marketplace for wholesale sourcing.

quiz.q: What is a 'bend-down' market?
options: A) A market where prices are fixed
B) A second-hand or thrift market
C) A market for new electronics
D) A wholesale market for food
quiz.explanation: In many African countries, 'bend-down' refers to second-hand or thrift markets.

quiz.q: Why should you go early to a thrift market?
options: A) To get the best items before they are picked
quiz.explanation: The best quality items are grabbed quickly, so going early gives you first pick.

quiz.q: Which brands are mentioned as selling fast on social media when sourced from thrift stores?
quiz.explanation: Zara, H&M, Nike, and Levi's are popular international brands that resell well.

quiz.q: What is a good strategy when buying from a garage sale?
options: A) Pay the asking price immediately
B) Negotiate for a discount on multiple items
quiz.explanation: Negotiating for a discount when buying multiple items can lower your cost.

quiz.q: Which of these is a popular online marketplace in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Kilimall is a popular online marketplace in Kenya.

quiz.q: What should you check before buying from an online seller on Alibaba?
options: C) The seller's social media followers
quiz.explanation: Checking seller ratings and reviews helps avoid scams and ensures quality.

quiz.q: What is a safe payment method when buying online from a stranger?
quiz.explanation: PayPal or escrow services protect your money if the goods are not as described.

quiz.q: What percentage discount should you aim for when buying 50 units from a supplier?
quiz.explanation: A 20-30% discount is a reasonable target for bulk purchases.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of paying cash during negotiation?
options: B) Suppliers often lower the price
C) You get a tax refund
D) You can return items anytime
quiz.explanation: Cash payment is immediate and risk-free for the supplier, so they may offer a better price.

quiz.q: What is group buying?
options: A) Buying from a group of suppliers
B) Pooling money with other resellers to buy in larger quantities
C) Buying only from social media groups
D) Selling to a group of customers
quiz.explanation: Group buying means teaming up with other resellers to buy a larger lot at a lower price.

quiz.q: What should you always get in writing after a negotiation?
options: B) The agreed price, quantity, and delivery date
D) A receipt for a deposit
quiz.explanation: A written record via WhatsApp or email prevents misunderstandings later.

quiz.q: When evaluating product quality, what should you check for clothes?
options: A) Fabric thickness, seams, and zippers
quiz.explanation: Fabric thickness, seams, and zippers are key indicators of clothing quality.

quiz.q: What is a good rule for setting your selling price?
options: A) Selling price should be at least double your total cost
B) Selling price should equal your cost
C) Selling price should be 10% above cost
D) Selling price should be tripled always
quiz.explanation: Doubling your total cost ensures a healthy profit margin after expenses.

quiz.q: Why is seasonality important in product selection?
options: B) It determines demand for certain products
C) It changes the quality of goods
quiz.explanation: Products like umbrellas sell more in rainy seasons, so demand varies by season.

quiz.q: What should you do if an item doesn't sell within 2 weeks?
options: B) Discount it to recover cash
quiz.explanation: Discounting slow-moving items helps recover cash and avoid dead stock.

quiz.q: What is a recommended tool for tracking inventory?
options: A) A notebook or Google Sheets
quiz.explanation: A notebook or free app like Google Sheets helps keep accurate records.

quiz.q: How should you store clothes to avoid wrinkles?
options: A) In plastic bins or hung
B) In a pile on the floor
quiz.explanation: Plastic bins or hanging prevents wrinkles and damage.

quiz.q: What is FIFO in inventory management?
quiz.explanation: FIFO means selling older stock first to avoid expiration or obsolescence.

quiz.q: When should you reorder stock?
options: A) When stock drops to 10 units
B) When stock is completely finished
C) Every month regardless of sales
D) Only when you have a sale
quiz.explanation: Setting a reorder point like 10 units ensures you don't run out of popular items.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of insuring high-value inventory?
options: A) It protects against loss or theft
D) It gives you free storage
quiz.explanation: Insurance covers financial loss if inventory is stolen or damaged.

quiz.q: Which of these is a local classifieds platform in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Jiji (formerly OLX) is a popular local classifieds platform in Nigeria.

quiz.q: What should you do before buying electronics from a thrift store?
quiz.explanation: Testing electronics ensures they function before you pay.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when buying in bulk?
options: A) Buying low-quality items that won't sell
quiz.explanation: Low-quality items may not sell, tying up your money in dead stock.

quiz.q: What should you factor into your total cost when calculating profit?
options: A) Purchase price, shipping, customs, packaging, ads
quiz.explanation: All these costs affect your final profit, so include them in your calculation.

quiz.q: Why is building a relationship with a supplier important?
options: A) You may get credit or better prices
B) They will give you free products
C) They will promote your business
D) They will deliver for free always
quiz.explanation: Good relationships can lead to credit terms and discounts on future orders.
